reasons: The lake identity record names Rehberg v. Paulk, court U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2012-04-02, year 2012, docket No. 10-788.
The lake citation record lists official citation 566 U.S. 356, parallels 132 S. Ct. 1497 and 182 L. Ed. 2d 593, and vendor citation 2012 U.S. LEXIS 2711.
The opinion's stated holding is that a grand jury witness receives the same absolute immunity under §1983 as a trial witness.
The case is centrally about the scope of absolute immunity for grand-jury testimony, including law-enforcement witnesses, so the Absolute Immunity anchor role is supported.
residual_risks: The corpus taxonomy meaning of Anchor is not independently defined in the disclosed files, but the legal fit is strong from the opinion text.

defect.evidence_quote: this rule may not be circumvented by claiming that a grand jury witness conspired to present false testimony or by using evidence of the witness’ testimony to support any other §1983 claim concerning the initiation or maintenance of a prosecution
defect.locator_note: holding/frontmatter; supported by opinion text at the paragraph beginning 'For these reasons, we conclude that grand jury witnesses should enjoy the same immunity as witnesses at trial.'
defect.problem: The holding is directionally supported but slightly overbroad: the Court barred use of grand-jury testimony to support other §1983 claims only when those claims concern the initiation or maintenance of a prosecution. The page says 'another § 1983 theory' without that qualifier.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise the final clause to: 'or by using evidence of the testimony to support another §1983 claim concerning the initiation or maintenance of a prosecution.' Consider describing the complaining-witness point as an alleged or so-called complaining-witness role, because the Court rejected that characterization for modern grand-jury witnesses.

reasons: The core proposition is supported: the opinion says grand-jury witnesses have absolute immunity from §1983 claims based on their testimony.
The opinion also supports applying the rule to law-enforcement witnesses and rejecting a conspiracy workaround.
The disclosed text contains an express limitation, 'concerning the initiation or maintenance of a prosecution,' that the page's holding omits.
residual_risks: The assertion remains usable if narrowed to testimony-based claims and prosecution-initiation or prosecution-maintenance theories.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add the prosecution-initiation/maintenance qualifier and avoid implying that non-testimonial complaining-witness conduct receives absolute immunity.

reasons: Lens A does not review treatment or currency.
The disclosed lake identity confirms the case is a U.S. Supreme Court decision, which supports the page's SCOTUS weight label as framed.
residual_risks: No Lens B treatment/currency review was performed.
